sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by FLAG/HA antibody binding on non-permeabilized (intact) cells in multiple independent studies; pulse-chase metabolic labeling confirms trafficking to the cell surface. Electrophysiology of the epitope-tagged channel itself is NOT MEASURED in the cited ledger lines.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names the junction as between S116 and K117 in human Kir2.1, placing the insert 10 residues from the TM1 C-boundary (residue 106) and 39 residues from the TM2 N-boundary (residue 156), well within the single extracellular loop (107–155). Python verification confirms residue 116 = S and residue 117 = K in the canonical sequence. L10 independently confirms the FLAG tag occupies positions 116–123 and is surface-accessible by antibody labeling. Multiple additional ledger lines (L2, L3, L7, L8) using HA tags in the same extracellular loop of full-length membrane-anchored Kir2.1 further corroborate that this loop tolerates short epitope insertions without disrupting surface trafficking. Full-length human Kir2.1 (KCNJ2) with a FLAG tag inserted between S116 and K117 in the single extracellular loop (topology landmarks: extracellular 107–155), expressed in mammalian cells. L10 (PMC9951526) independently confirms the FLAG occupies positions 116–123 and that antibody labeling is disrupted by mutations at those positions, corroborating extracellular accessibility. L2/L3 (PMC3139129) and L7/L8 (PMC12775956) report HA-tagged full-length Kir2.1 with the tag in the same extracellular loop, confirmed by antibody binding on non-permeabilized cells and pulse-chase trafficking assays. L4/L5 (PMC9273215) report the same loop insertion in mouse Kir2.1 citing Stockklausner et al. 2001 (the same original reference cited in L1 for the S116–K117 junction), providing indirect ortholog support for this junction.

sources.claim: FLAG tag epitopes were added into previously described extracellular loops of Kir2.1 (between S116 and K117 59 ), Kir3.1 (between K114 and A115 56 ), Asic1a (between F147 and K148 103 ), and P2X 3 (between N72 and R73 based on insertion into the paralog P2X 2 104 ).
